# read_B: pp. 75–77 (images n76–n78), established from the images

## Line counts and method
- p. 75 (n76) has five lines. It is a leaf front and opens with ༄༅༔, a gap, then ༔ (checked at ×3).
- p. 76 (n77) has five lines. It is a leaf back, with no ornament.
- p. 77 (n78) has five lines. It is a leaf front and opens with ༄༅༔ ༔ (checked).
- In all there are 15 print lines. The witness's line breaks match the print on 15 of 15.

The scans are tilted: n76 by +1.25°, n77 by −1.4° and n78 by +1.35°. Each page was deskewed first. The angle was the one that maximised the sharpness of the row profile.

Headlines after deskewing: n76 at y≈132/188/244/300/356; n77 at y≈136/196/248/304/356; n78 at y≈132/188/244/300/356.

Each line was cropped in four overlapping segments at ×3 (LANCZOS). Doubtful syllables were enlarged ×6–×12. A pixel dump (threshold 128) was made for every line end and for the tsheg questions.

Filler dots in mid-line are left out. There is a run of them in 75.1 (ལ་…ཆད) and a double mark after 76.1 མ་ (taken as a tsheg). The blank stretches in 75.5 (after དབང་གིས༔ and after བྲོས་ནས༔) are empty block, not lost text.

Tsheg before ༔: the five ངོ་༔ (75.1 ×2, 75.4, 75.5, 76.3) were compared in one montage (×5). Three show a separate dot between ངོ and ༔. In 75.1 (first) and 75.5 the dot is fused to the tail of ངོ. The witness's ངོ་༔ is kept in all five.

## [?] (3)
- **75.1 བྱེད[?]** (witness བྱེད; the other recension has ཕྱེད). At ×10 the head of the stack cannot be told apart between བ and ཕ: it has a notch at top left, but no clear ཕ-hook like the one in 75.3 ཕྱམ. Context (གར | སྣ་ཚོགས་བྱེད་ཅིང, "performing various dances") supports བྱེད. Taken from the witness.
- **76.3 བཅས[?]**: after དང་ the prefix letter is open, like a ང, with no closed box. This is probably a worn བ. Taken from the witness (དང་བཅས, as in the other recension).
- **77.5 ཚོཌ[?]**: after ཚོ stands one reversed-looking letter, with its stem at the left and its bar running right. The witness reads it as ཌ, and the image does not contradict that. No ས follows. The sense needs ཚོགས (see misprints).

Close calls not marked [?]:
- 75.2 (line end) མེར་: the head bar of ར runs 5 px past the stem and tapers below. This is read as a fused tsheg (witness kept).
- 75.3 (line end) སྙིང་: the head of ང runs into the frame. A 6 px swelling sits on the rule at headline height, which may be a fused tsheg. The witness's tsheg is kept. If the drafter reads none, use `# fix: ཐད་སྙིངཀར་མིག => ཐད་སྙིང་ཀར་མིག`.
- 77.2 (line end) བདག་: the head of ག runs into a thickened frame, and no separate blob can be seen. The witness's tsheg is kept. If the drafter reads none: `# fix: ཀྱིས༔ བདགདག་པ => ཀྱིས༔ བདག་དག་པ`.
- 76.1 དེ་ཙན: ཙ and ན touch, and no tsheg can be seen. Kept as the witness has it, with a fix below.

The line-join fixes are 75.1→75.2, 76.3→76.4, 77.1→77.2 and 77.3→77.4. None of these joins crosses a page ornament. The joins 75.5→76.1 and 76.5→77.1 both have a tsheg, so the 76.5 → ༄༅༔ ༔བས join needs no fix.

No line-end abbreviations (པའཾ, ལཾ, ནམཁའ) occur. One subscript-ས ligature does: 77.5 ལྕགྶ.

## Tsheg status of my first and last lines
- First line (75.1) ends ཀྱི with **no** tsheg, so it needs a fix.
- Last line (77.5) ends ལྕགྶ་ **with** a tsheg. It continues on p. 78 (Reader C), presumably with ཀྱུས.

## Suspected misprints
1. **75.5 དུད་འགྲེའི** should be འགྲོའི, "of the animals", as at 75.4, 76.4 and 76.5. The sense allows only one reading. Certainty of the print's reading is moderate (the second o-stroke might be worn away). Proposed `# fix: དུད་འགྲེའི => དུད་འགྲོའི` (rule 5b).
2. **77.4 བདེ་གཤིགས** should be བདེ་གཤེགས, "sugata". Only one reading is possible. Certainty is moderate to high: the vowel was compared against ཤིག and ཤེས on n77. Proposed `# fix: བདེ་གཤིགས => བདེ་གཤེགས`.
3. **77.5 ལྷ་ཚོཌ** should be ལྷ་ཚོགས, "assembly of deities". Only one reading is possible. Proposed `# fix: ལྷ་ཚོཌ => ལྷ་ཚོགས`.
4. 77.5 ཨ་ཙ་མ་ར: the usual exclamation is ཨ་ཙ་མ་རེ (the witness), and the other recension has ཨ་ཙ་མ. The sense does not depend on it, so it is **kept, note only**.

Not misprints: the print's own spelling and wording, such as གཏོད, མདུན་བརྩེ་གཅིག (for འདུན་པ་རྩེ་གཅིག), བཀོལ་གཅོད and སྐྱེས་སྟེ.
